name: Executive order of August 15, 1883 setting apart the Iowa Reservation in Indian Territory
promises: The order set apart a reservation in Indian Territory for the Iowa (Royce; Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma).
today: The Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma says its original reservation in Oklahoma was established by this order and that Iowas who wished to stay on the northern lands were allowed to. How the reservation was later reduced is a separate event.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says its original Oklahoma reservation was established by executive order of August 15, 1883, after some Ioways were moved to Indian Territory.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 912

openQuestions: This order created a reservation and took no land; no finding about it was located.
treaties.json also lists the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska; the 1883 reserve was for the Iowa in Indian Territory, today the Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma.
The Commission's Iowa dockets were not searched for findings on the 1890 agreement that later reduced this reservation; that belongs to its own record.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Iowa, Iowa August 15 1883. Found Iowa Tribe of Indians v. United States, 68 Ct. Cl. 585 (December 2, 1929), https://static.case.law/us-ct-cl/68/cases/0585-01.json: it recites this order as the source of the reservation, then holds that the 1890 Jerome Commission agreement ceding its surplus land (about 38 cents an acre) left out an oral promise of the price paid to neighbouring tribes, and awards $254,632.59. That is a finding about the 1890 cession of this reservation, a later event, so it is not counted on this record.

Resolved 2026-11-08: the 1890 Jerome agreement, ratified by the Act of February 13, 1891 (26 Stat. 749, Iowa text at 753-758), now has its own record, cession-1891-02-13-iowa (split from this one by a treaty-corrections.json entry, area 649, since Royce lists no Iowa row for 1891). The 1929 Court of Claims finding and award are recorded there.
